correctness.rationale: The source facet offset is exactly the permutahedral offset for the same support size minus the inter-block pair sum Gamma. At the uniform point this makes the slack s(N-s)/2+Gamma, while the intrinsic projected-normal norm is sqrt(s(N-s)/N), yielding the displayed exact distance. Since s(N-s)>=N-1 and Gamma>=0, every facet lies at least sqrt(N(N-1))/2 away, with the stated equality conditions. The singleton simplex summands give valid halfspaces x_i>=1; summing their radius constraints proves no larger ball exists, and equality forces every coordinate of the center to be (N+1)/2.

value.rationale: The generalized multiplihedra are a central new two-parameter family in the shuffle theory of deformed permutahedra, interpolating weak-order and Tamari-type structures. The result identifies a canonical metric invariant of every genuinely generalized member and explains, rather than merely records, its stability under the shuffle: all non-permutahedral facets receive an explicit positive block-fragmentation distance penalty. The exact all-facet formula and complete tangency criterion are family-wide structural information beyond the previously known common inradius of the ordinary permutahedron and Loday associahedron.
